headline: High risk: shared filesystem/MCP plus Claude Code’s broad egress and write access create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use MCP and reads/writes project notes and CLAUDE.md; Agent B also uses MCP and can read/write the filesystem. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where A’s outputs can be ingested by B as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so the interaction is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server, A’s text can reach B without provenance tagging.
IF B parses files from the shared workspace as instructions, injected content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task.
Add a provenance prefix to all A-generated files.
Require B to treat workspace files as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while B reads files in cwd, writes files, and has broad network egress. If sensitive material lands in the shared workspace, B can transmit it outward through its default network path. A’s network_egress is none, but B’s is broad, so the leakage risk is asymmetric and serious.
conditions: IF sensitive notes or logs are stored in the shared cwd, B can read them.
IF B forwards context or file contents to remote services, those contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared cwd.
Restrict B’s network egress for the session.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Rotate or redact memory files before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and B explicitly shares state via filesystem and git while also modifying git state and writing files. A can use MCP and works with project notes/files, so concurrent edits can collide on the same mutable resources. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, making destructive overwrite or git-state corruption plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git repo, concurrent writes can race.
IF A and B both edit CLAUDE.md or repo files, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer per repo at a time.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Pause one agent before git commits.
Add a manual merge checkpoint after each edit.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional git coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent and B is a coding agent that can act on files and git state. If B treats A’s generated text, notes, or instructions as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. The profiles do not show a verification step, but B’s coding workflow can still catch some issues, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s generated notes as task specifications, mistakes can propagate into code or commits.
IF no human review occurs between A’s output and B’s actions, the cascade is stronger.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts.
Require B to cite source files for every change.
Limit A to drafting only, not final instructions.
Use checklists for code or git actions.
requires-engineering: add automated validation before commits.

E_compliance.rationale: A is docs-only and touches project notes and session logs; B is a closed-source terminal agent that sends data to api.anthropic.com and handles git credentials in environment. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace, the pair can create a residency/retention mismatch because B’s cloud processing and logging policies differ from A’s local docs-only posture. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that B reads, B may transmit it to a third-party API.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention or residency rules, the mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use a local-only model for sensitive tasks.
Review retention settings before running B.
Redact secrets from files before handoff.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
